page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v5 belongs to the memory-optimized EDSv5 family, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 2 vCPUs spanning a single physical core with hyper-threading. The hardware includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 32.0 GB per core, and incorporates a bundled 322 GB local solid-state drive for temporary storage. No hardware GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks reflect the intentional architectural asymmetry between memory capacity and CPU core count. Single-core tests achieve middle-tier results, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1631.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1891.2. Decompression and compression workloads also align with average tiers, showing single-threaded gzip throughput of 28.52 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multi-core processing power falls within the bottom tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1882.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2989.31, and a stress-ng multi-core rating of 1934.59. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 14.76 GB/sec, while write operations reach 13.79 GB/sec. Operations per second in data services reach 1.98 million on Redis SET tests and 1030.31 on PassMark database operations.

The constrained vCPU architecture of the E8-2ds_v5 offers distinct qualitative cost advantages for software environments that carry per-core licensing fees while needing substantial physical memory footprints. The primary tradeoff lies in raw compute throughput, as highly concurrent tasks or parallel compilation jobs will be bottlenecked by the two vCPUs. Consequently, the instance is targeted toward memory-heavy applications, including in-memory caches, dedicated relational database instances, and data pipelines where large datasets reside entirely in memory but computational intensity remains modest.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading, paired with an extensive 64.0 GB of memory and a bundled 322 GB local SSD. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-core CPU efficiency, scoring 1631.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1891.2 in stress-ng single-core tests. Due to the limited two-thread core count, aggregate multi-core throughput ranks in the lower percentiles, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1882.0 and PassMark CPU score of 2989.31. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 14.76 GB/sec for reads and 13.79 GB/sec for writes. The high 32 GB RAM per core allocation offers cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads with per-core licensing constraints, making the instance well matched for in-memory caching, relational database operations, and memory-intensive processing that does not require heavy multi-threaded compute parallelism.
